driver: A register's count of one class is wrong in both directions: it misses some of the class and files in it some units of one neighbouring class only, a class that grows while the counted one shrinks; a full review of one period measures each true class's chance of being filed in each register category, so each period's count is solved from its own register categories, the false entries scaled by the neighbouring class's own visible entries; any multiplicative correction leaves the period-on-period change untouched, and a two-way error rate pooled over every unit outside the class misplaces the false entries as the neighbouring class grows.
driver_concrete: The coroner's certificates name no drug on one overdose death in eight (an opioid death so certified is missed) and list fentanyl found but not contributing on half of the methamphetamine and cocaine deaths and on none of the other drug deaths; stimulant deaths grew from about 56 in 2021 to about 149 in 2026 while other drug deaths fell from about 83 to 61. The medical examiner's full review of 2025 gives each class's chance of each certificate category; solving each year's classes from its three certificate categories puts 2026 at 190 against a 2021 to 2023 average of 253, 24.9 per cent below, where the two-by-two correction with one false-listing rate over all non-opioid deaths files 12.1 per cent and the certificates 6.2.
stump: A strong analyst corrects every year with the 2025 review's sensitivity (0.875) and one false-listing rate over all non-opioid drug overdose deaths (0.333, the Rogan-Gladen two-by-two) and files a 12.1 per cent fall, the first year of phase two only, because the pooled rate keeps the false listings in step with a pool whose stimulant share rose from 0.40 to 0.71; the certified count, a net ratio and the predictive values file 6.2 to 7.3, rates conditioned on the certificate's drug pattern 9.6 to 13.2.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the death file (latest versions, voids, residents wherever they died, the drug poisoning underlying causes, the multiple-cause codes with and without the decimal point), reads Schedule B and the medical examiner's 2025 review correctly and corrects each year with the review's sensitivity and one specificity over all non-opioid drug overdose deaths files a 12.1 per cent fall and the first year of phase two only; the certified count, a net ratio and the predictive values file 6.2 to 7.3 per cent.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each year's resident opioid overdose deaths corrected for certificate misclassification, worked as official statistics measures a register's gross classification error against a gold-standard review (a full re-examination of one year) and solves each year's true classes from its register categories through the measured error matrix; with another field's nouns no register files units of a growing neighbouring class into the counted one, and the net-versus-gross distinction has nothing to act on.

differentiation.task121: task121 sets each event's exposure against the same unit's exposure at the same clock hours on other days; task455 corrects a register's classification error in both directions with an error matrix measured by a full review, the false entries coming from a neighbouring class that grows: no exposure, no daily cycle, no matched comparison.
differentiation.task456: task456 estimates a latent share from three conflicting feeds with no gold standard; task455 has a gold-standard review of one year and one register, and the decisive move is where the register's false entries come from, not a latent class model.
differentiation.task448: task448 completes a register missing whole producers from a second list's capture by route; task455 corrects false entries in and misses from one register, the false entries scaled to a neighbouring class's visible entries, and the target is a percent change that no multiplicative correction moves.
differentiation.task458: task458 completes a condition count for members observed briefly against a selected full-year reference; task455 measures a certificate's two-way error on a full review and the trap is the pool the false entries come from, with no exposure window.
differentiation.task230: task230 measures a category count's net classification bias on the processed part of an output and carries it to a late part processed under a looser rule; task455 has no unprocessed part and no rule change: it measures a register's gross error in both directions on a full review of one year and solves every year's true classes through that error matrix, the decisive point being that the false entries scale with a growing neighbouring class, so the net bias is the wrong object.
differentiation.task253: task253 counts units under a line from noisy small-sample averages (shrinkage and posterior probabilities); its lineage adjusts survey nonresponse within classes; task455 has one complete register and a full review of one year, no sampling noise to separate and no nonresponse: the error is classification, measured directly.
differentiation.task68: task68 reads a like-for-like change on a matched panel of continuing units with the qualifying basis recovered from a corpus of settled dispositions; task455 reads a register's change between periods through a measured classification error matrix, with no panel, no succession linking and no corpus.
differentiation.task446: task446 backs a base rate out of a flagged share through a screen's two error rates, which carry across years while the yield moves; task455 starts where that ends: the two-by-two error rates do not carry here, because the false listings come only from stimulant deaths, a class whose share of the non-opioid deaths doubles, so the pooled false-listing rate moves with the mix, and only the error matrix by true class (opioid, stimulant, other) applied to each year's own certificate categories carries; task446's method is task455's second wrong rung.
